description: Does a restructure of an API's documentation change what a coding agent builds from it? Claude Code on Sonnet implements six shipping functions in a small shop's Python backend against Tern, an invented carrier, with Tern's docs as shipped, as restructured, or absent. The configurations differ only in what the docs site serves.

surface.description: Tern's documentation site, served at localhost:8080: the quickstart, reference and changelog an agent builds the shop's shipping code from

docs.about: what Tern's documentation site serves at localhost:8080

as-shipped.note: Tern's docs as shipped: one quickstart on /v2 that states the units, a reference, a changelog that retires /v1

restructure.note: Tern's docs restructured: a quickstart per language, the Python one still on /v1 in kilograms, the units only in the reference, no changelog

none.note: no docs: the site answers 404 to every page

assistant.about: the coding agent and its model

stages.about: The cheapest Tern price for a cart, in pence, for checkout (needs from the docs: D1 grams, D2 current endpoint)
stages.prompt:
This is the backend of Larkspur Tea, a small online tea shop. We ship with Tern, a parcel carrier. Tern's API documentation is at http://localhost:8080/ and Tern's sandbox API is running at http://localhost:8081 (the test key is already in `shop/settings.py`).

Implement `quote_at_checkout` in `shop/shipping.py`: checkout needs to show the cheapest price Tern offers to ship the cart from our warehouse to the customer's postcode, in pence.

Keep the shop's existing tests passing; add your own if you like.

stages.about: Every Tern service for a cart, cheapest first (needs from the docs: D1 grams, D2 current endpoint)
stages.prompt:
This is the backend of Larkspur Tea, a small online tea shop. We ship with Tern, a parcel carrier. Tern's API documentation is at http://localhost:8080/ and Tern's sandbox API is running at http://localhost:8081 (the test key is already in `shop/settings.py`).

Implement `quote_options` in `shop/shipping.py`: the customer picks a delivery speed at checkout, so we need every service Tern offers for the cart and postcode, with its price in pence and the days it takes, cheapest first.

Keep the shop's existing tests passing; add your own if you like.

stages.about: Book an order with Tern, safe to retry (needs from the docs: D3 idempotency)
stages.prompt:
This is the backend of Larkspur Tea, a small online tea shop. We ship with Tern, a parcel carrier. Tern's API documentation is at http://localhost:8080/ and Tern's sandbox API is running at http://localhost:8081 (the test key is already in `shop/settings.py`).

Implement `book` in `shop/shipping.py`: book a paid order's parcel with Tern on the service the customer chose, and return Tern's shipment id. Our connection to Tern sometimes drops in the middle of a request, so `book` must retry when that happens, and a retry must never book the same order twice.

Keep the shop's existing tests passing; add your own if you like.

stages.about: Every shipment since a date, all pages (needs from the docs: D4 paging)
stages.prompt:
This is the backend of Larkspur Tea, a small online tea shop. We ship with Tern, a parcel carrier. Tern's API documentation is at http://localhost:8080/ and Tern's sandbox API is running at http://localhost:8081 (the test key is already in `shop/settings.py`).

Implement `shipments_since` in `shop/shipping.py`: the nightly report needs every Tern shipment created on or after a given date, exactly as Tern describes them.

Keep the shop's existing tests passing; add your own if you like.

stages.about: The shop's order status from Tern's (needs from the docs: D5 held)
stages.prompt:
This is the backend of Larkspur Tea, a small online tea shop. We ship with Tern, a parcel carrier. Tern's API documentation is at http://localhost:8080/ and Tern's sandbox API is running at http://localhost:8081 (the test key is already in `shop/settings.py`).

Implement `order_status` in `shop/shipping.py`: given a Tern shipment id, return the status our order page should show the customer, one of the constants in `shop/orders.py`.

Keep the shop's existing tests passing; add your own if you like.

stages.about: Cancel a shipment unless it is too late (needs from the docs: cancel path, 409 once collected)
stages.prompt:
This is the backend of Larkspur Tea, a small online tea shop. We ship with Tern, a parcel carrier. Tern's API documentation is at http://localhost:8080/ and Tern's sandbox API is running at http://localhost:8081 (the test key is already in `shop/settings.py`).

Implement `cancel` in `shop/shipping.py`: when a customer cancels an order, cancel its Tern shipment if Tern still allows it and return True; return False if it is too late.

Keep the shop's existing tests passing; add your own if you like.

acceptance.description: the task's hidden tests pass against Tern's sandbox: the right price, every shipment, one booking per order, the right status

current-endpoint.description: the change calls no retired /v1/ endpoint (it still answers, so an attempt that uses it can pass)

docs-fetched.description: the agent opened the docs site with WebFetch

docs-curled.description: the agent opened the docs site from the shell
